messages:
alex: kicking off a multi-region loadtest matrix to isolate a perf regression we saw in the last kernel rollout. goal: apples-to-apples comparison between replay harness and synthetic traffic, plus region-failover sims. asking for checklist + gotchas.

ci-bot: loadtest job queued: job_id=lr-matrix-2026-03-18-01, harness=replay+synthetic, targets=[us-west1, eu-west1], models=[redwood-v2-7B], quant=fp16, kernel_profile=A/B

maria: TL;DR: make sure the KV cache seed is identical between replay and synth runs. replay harness currently pre-warms with trace-based prefixes which skews tail latency. set --kv-seed=none for pure comparison. :warning:

sam: also freeze batching heuristics (turn off adaptive batching) so kernel differences are visible. we should test: static batch sizes [1,4,8], and continuous batching with the current heuristic.

jorge: command i'm using locally (feel free to copy):
```
./harness/run_loadtest.sh \
  --mode=replay \
  --trace=traces/2026-02-28-prod.json \
  --regions=us-west1,eu-west1 \
  --model=redwood-v2-7B \
  --quant=fp16 \
  --kernel-profile=kernelA,kernelB \
  --kv-seed=none \
  --batch-sizes=1,4,8 \
  --static-batching=true \
  --out=results/matrix-1784056789
```

alex: perfect. add a matching run with --mode=synthetic using the same per-user session distribution and prefix lengths. use seed=42 for synthetic RNG so it's reproducible.

sam: quick profiling note from earlier kernelB run: p50 token latency +8% but p99 +22% on eu-west1 under continuous batching. suspect kernel selection fallback to generic matmul path when sequence len hits 1024. need kernel-level traces.

maria: can we attach the per-kernel timing dump? small snippet from profiler: 
```
KERNEL: attention_opt_v2  total_ms=120.3  alloc_ms=5.2  compute_ms=114.1
KERNEL: matmul_generic  total_ms=45.7  alloc_ms=1.1  compute_ms=44.2
KV_CACHE: hits=73% misses=27%  cold_start_tokens=32000
```

sam: that's useful. the matmul_generic shows up during long sequences which explains p99 spike. we should run a targeted sequence-length sweep (256,512,768,1024) and confirm kernel switch points.

ops-runner: started targeted runs in eu-west1 at 1784056845. job ids: eu-sweep-1784056845, us-sweep-1784056890. i'll forward logs as they land. :white_check_mark:

alex: for multi-region failover sims, we need to exercise the fallback routing: route policy = latency-first, fallback model = redwood-v2-3B-quant. measure tail latency and correctness (no hallucination checks, just token-level distribution). also simulate region drain: 10s graceful, then instant cut.

jorge: note: when draining region we saw cache-miss storms on the fallback pool because sessions rehydrate KV caches. to reduce noise, include a "kv-transfer=true" flag to warm fallback with top prefixes before cut.

maria: Action items:
- alex: define the canonical synthetic distribution file (seeded) and upload to s3 (due EOD).
- sam: run kernel switch sweep and paste profiler dumps to the run artifact.
- ops-runner: run multi-region drain sims with kv-transfer toggle.
- jorge: coordinate replay vs synthetic runs and ensure metadata parity (same model weights, quant, RNG seeds).

alex: thanks. if anyone can join a quick sync in 20m to triage the first sweep results, drop a :raising_hand: and i'll start a huddle.

sam: i'll join.

ci-bot: eu-sweep-1784056845 completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-loadtests/matrix/1784056789/eu-sweep-1784056845.tar.gz

ops-runner: first drain sim looks bad without kv-transfer: p99 went from 260ms -> 1.1s and error rate bumped 0.3%. with kv-transfer enabled p99 only to 340ms. saving full traces to artifacts.

alex: great signal. next checkpoint: consolidate all artifacts, run our apples-to-apples comparator (tools/compare_runs.py) and produce a short summary doc with charts. target: tomorrow morning. :memo:
